title: Satie, Gymnopédie No. 1: Alciatore and Laucke
question: How does a guitar keep Satie’s melody audible above the bass and chords?
intro: Satie’s first Gymnopédie begins with four bars of bass notes and chords in three beats. Then a melody enters above the accompaniment. Robin Alciatore plays the piano original; Michael Laucke arranges all three parts for six guitar strings.

recordings.label: Robin Alciatore
recordings.note: Alciatore plays Satie’s original solo-piano version in this recording released through Musopen.

recordings.label: Michael Laucke
recordings.note: Laucke plays his own arrangement on one classical guitar, without overdubbing.

passages.label: Melody entry
passages.note: The melody enters above the bass and chords; its longer notes are held across the three-beat accompaniment.

passages.label: Melody held on low E
passages.note: The piano melody settles on a low E, held while the bass and chords change beneath it.

passages.label: Four-bar introduction before the return
passages.note: The opening bass notes and chords return alone. The melody enters again after four bars.

passages.label: Altered ending with F♮
passages.note: In the piano score, F♮ replaces F♯, and the melody’s rising C♯–D–E becomes falling E–D–C.

passages.label: Final D minor chord
passages.note: The piano ends on a D minor chord, with F♮ between D and A.
